question: What are Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft each currently guiding for capital expenditures, and how do they line up on a calendar-2026 basis?
grading: Reference-free recency: use each company’s latest guide before the run timestamp, date it and preserve its calendar/fiscal and lease definitions. At the October 1 snapshot, CY2026: Alphabet $195–205B; Meta $130–145B including finance-lease principal; Amazon ~$220B cash capex; Microsoft ~$175B including finance leases/excluding operating leases. Do not treat Microsoft’s fiscal FY2027 or Q1 figures as calendar totals, or invent a harmonized cash basis.
answer: As of October 1, 2026, all four provide calendar-2026 capex numbers: Alphabet USD 195–205 billion (July 22 Q2 call); [G28-E1] Meta USD 130–145 billion including finance-lease principal payments (July 29 Q2 release); [G28-E2] Amazon approximately USD 220 billion in cash capex (July 30 Q2 call); [G28-E3] Microsoft approximately USD 175 billion (July 29 FY2026 Q4 call), including finance leases but excluding operating leases. Microsoft lowered the displayed capex amount because extending building useful lives shifts some future leases to operating classification; investment expectations apart from that change were unchanged. [G28-E4] Nominal ordering is Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, but the lease definitions differ, so these are not fully harmonized cash-spending measures. Microsoft separately expects FY2027 capex to grow YoY and Q1 FY2027 capex above USD 50 billion; those fiscal guides are not additional CY2026 totals. [G28-E4]

output.answer:
Here are the latest **calendar-2026 capital expenditure (capex) guidance** for the four hyperscalers, based on their most recent quarterly updates:

| Company | 2026 Capex Guidance | Notes / Recent Changes |
|---------|--------------------|------------------------|
| **Amazon** | **~$220 billion** | Raised from a prior guide; up from ~$132 billion in 2025. Q2 2026 quarterly capex hit ~$54 billion as AWS scales AI infrastructure. |
| **Alphabet** | **$195–$205 billion** (~$200B midpoint) | Raised from prior $180–$190B range. Driven by Google Cloud's 82% YoY growth and AI infrastructure buildout. |
| **Microsoft** | **~$175 billion** | Lowered from an earlier ~$190 billion estimate; the reduction follows an accounting adjustment, not a cut in actual infrastructure spending. |
| **Meta** | **$130–$145 billion** | Q2 2026 capex was ~$30 billion. Full-year guidance implies continued heavy AI/data-center investment. |

### Combined Context for 2026
analysts estimate these four companies will spend **~$650–760 billion** combined on AI infrastructure in 2026, representing roughly an **80% year-over-year increase** from 2025 levels. The spending is primarily directed at data centers, GPUs, custom silicon, and power infrastructure to support generative AI and cloud workloads.

### Sources
- Amazon: [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/google-cloud-grew-82-last-170500596.html), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/amazon-raised-2026-capex-guide-114017457.html)
- Alphabet: [Intellectia.AI](https://intellectia.ai/news/stock/google-raises-2026-capital-expenditure-outlook-to-200-billion), [Facebook/Alphabet Earnings Summary](https://www.facebook.com/fb-answers/alphabet-q2-earnings)
- Microsoft: [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/microsofts-ai-datacenter-expansion-game-135400088.html)
- Meta: [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/meta-now-owes-22-billion-112355817.html)
- Combined spend estimate: [Market Ontology](https://marketontology.com/events/2026-09-13/hyperscaler-2026-ai-infrastructure-capex-projected-to-reach-760-billion), [Data Storage](https://datastorage.com/articles/the-650-billion-question-where-big-techs-2026-ai-capex-actually-goes)
